sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: JavaScript questions dominate the frontend round of any fullstack interview. Java developers often underestimate JS because it looks syntactically similar, but the language behaves very differently: variables hoist, functions are first-class objects, `this` changes based on call context, and the entire async model is event-loop based rather than thread-based. Mastering these differences is what separates a backend developer who knows some JS from a genuine fullstack developer.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **Hoisting**: `var` declarations move to the top of their function scope; `let`/`const` stay in a temporal dead zone.
- **Closures**: a function retains access to its outer scope even after that scope has returned — this is how module patterns and counters work.
- **`this` is dynamic**: in regular functions, `this` is set by *how* the function is called, not where it is defined. Arrow functions fix `this` to the enclosing lexical scope.
- **Event loop**: JS is single-threaded. The call stack runs synchronous code; async callbacks sit in a queue and are picked up only when the stack is empty.
- **Promises/async-await**: async-await is syntactic sugar over Promises. Under the hood, every `await` is a `.then()` callback in the microtask queue.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **variables-scope-hoisting**: know exactly what `var`, `let`, `const` each do and what temporal dead zone means.
- **closures-and-iife**: be able to explain a closure in plain English and draw the loop + setTimeout closure trap.
- **arrow-functions-this**: know when `this` breaks in a regular method vs arrow function, and how `bind/call/apply` differ.
- **event-loop-and-async**: be able to predict the output order of `console.log`, `setTimeout`, and `Promise.resolve().then()`.
- **promises-async-await**: know Promise states, `.then/.catch`, `Promise.all`, and async/await error handling.
- **comparisons**: `==` vs `===`, `null` vs `undefined`, `var` vs `let` vs `const` — these appear in every interview.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"What is the difference between `var`, `let`, and `const`?"* — scope (function vs block), hoisting, and mutability.
- *"What is a closure? Give an example."* — a function that captures variables from its outer scope.
- *"What is the event loop?"* — single-threaded JS processes a call stack; the event loop moves callbacks from the task/microtask queue to the stack when it's empty.
- *"What does `==` vs `===` mean?"* — `==` coerces types before comparing; `===` checks type AND value strictly.
- *"Explain `async/await` in terms a Java developer would understand."* — similar to CompletableFuture but syntactically synchronous-looking; runs on the event loop not a thread pool.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"JavaScript runs on a single thread. When you call an async function with `await`, execution pauses at that line and the function's continuation is queued as a microtask. The event loop picks it up once the current call stack is empty. This is fundamentally different from Java where async work runs on separate threads — in JS, blocking the call stack with a heavy synchronous loop will freeze the entire UI, which is why we always keep CPU-intensive work off the main thread or delegate it to Web Workers."*
